subject: Political Science (Code: 323)
past_paper_reference: CUET UG Political Science Past Papers (2022-2024)

questions.question: Under the national leadership of Jawaharlal Nehru, the Indian National Congress won how many seats in the first Lok Sabha elections of 1951-52?
options: A) 364 seats
B) 250 seats
C) 410 seats
D) 489 seats
questions.explanation: The Congress won 364 of the 489 seats in the first Lok Sabha, establishing an overwhelming parliamentary majority under Jawaharlal Nehru.

questions.sub_topic: Father of Modern Statistics in India
questions.question: Which visionary architect of India's Second Five Year Plan is widely celebrated as the 'Father of Modern Statistics in India'?
options: A) Dr. K.N. Raj
B) Professor P.C. Mahalanobis
C) Dr. Verghese Kurien
D) Dr. M.S. Swaminathan
questions.explanation: Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis is celebrated as the Father of Modern Statistics in India, and his birthday (29 June) is celebrated as National Statistics Day.

questions.question: The Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) was formally established on which date through the signing of the Bangkok Declaration?
options: A) 15 August 1947
B) 1 January 1993
C) 8 August 1967
D) 24 October 1945
questions.explanation: ASEAN was founded on 8 August 1967 in Bangkok, Thailand, by five founding Southeast Asian member states.

questions.sub_topic: Flight of the Nawab of Junagadh
questions.question: Following popular uprisings and the establishment of the Arzi Hukumat provisional government in 1947, Nawab Mahabat Khan III of Junagadh fled to:
options: A) London, United Kingdom
B) Hyderabad, Deccan
C) Kabul, Afghanistan
D) Karachi, Pakistan
questions.explanation: Facing popular revolt and economic isolation, the Nawab fled by air to Karachi in October 1947 with his family and treasury, leaving his Dewan Sir Shah Nawaz Bhutto in charge.

questions.question: In the second general elections of 1957, approximately how many Indian citizens were enrolled on the electoral rolls, making it the largest democratic exercise in the world?
options: A) Over 19.3 crore (193 million) voters
B) 5 crore voters
C) 50 crore voters
D) 90 crore voters
questions.explanation: The registered electorate expanded from 17.3 crore in 1952 to over 19.3 crore in 1957, demonstrating the institutional consolidation of universal adult franchise.

questions.question: The First Five Year Plan (1951-1956) allocated its largest share of public investment (over 31% of plan outlay) to:
options: A) Heavy industrial steel mills and capital machinery
B) Agriculture, community development, and irrigation projects
C) Nuclear power reactors and aerospace defense
D) Information technology and telecommunications
questions.explanation: The First Plan prioritized food self-sufficiency and post-Partition refugee rehabilitation, investing heavily in agriculture, canals, and multipurpose dams (like Bhakra Nangal and Damodar Valley).

questions.question: The Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence (Panchsheel) were formally signed by Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru and Premier Zhou Enlai in Beijing on:
options: A) 15 August 1947
B) 18 April 1955
C) 29 April 1954
D) 20 October 1962
questions.explanation: Panchsheel was signed on 29 April 1954 in the preamble to the Agreement on Trade and Intercourse between the Tibet Region of China and India.

questions.topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: Following the 1967 general elections, Congress lost power in how many state assemblies, leading to non-Congress SVD and coalition ministries across northern and eastern India?
options: A) Every single state across India
B) Only two states
C) Fifteen states
D) Nine states (seven directly at the polls and two via subsequent defections)
questions.explanation: The Congress lost assembly majorities in seven states (Punjab, Haryana, UP, Bihar, West Bengal, Orissa, Madras, and Kerala) and lost two more through post-election defections, losing control over nine states.

questions.question: In 1974, to coordinate the student agitations of Gujarat and Bihar into a nationwide struggle against corruption and price rise, Jayaprakash Narayan established the:
options: A) National Coordination Committee for Total Revolution
B) All India Socialist Workers Council
C) Janata Action Commission
D) Democratic Defense Front
questions.explanation: JP established the National Coordination Committee uniting non-communist opposition parties and student unions to lead the nationwide agitation for Total Revolution.

questions.question: Which prominent political leader who was appointed Governor of Punjab played a crucial mediating role in facilitating secret negotiations for the 1985 Rajiv-Longowal Accord?
options: A) Siddhartha Shankar Ray
B) Arjun Singh
C) B.D. Pande
D) S.S. Barnala
questions.explanation: Arjun Singh was appointed Governor of Punjab in March 1985 and worked as Rajiv Gandhi's chief political negotiator to broker the Memorandum of Settlement with Sant Longowal.

questions.question: Between 1981 and 1983, which veteran Chipko leader undertook a legendary 4,870-kilometre trans-Himalayan foot march from Kashmir to Kohima to spread ecological awareness?
options: A) Chandi Prasad Bhatt
B) Gaura Devi
C) Sunderlal Bahuguna
D) Amrita Devi Bishnoi
questions.explanation: Sunderlal Bahuguna walked across the entire Himalayan range from Kashmir to Kohima between 1981 and 1983, documenting forest destruction and popularizing the Chipko philosophy.

questions.question: In August 1990, the implementation of the Mandal Commission recommendations coincided with a fierce internal crisis in the National Front government that led to the sacking of:
options: A) Finance Minister Madhu Dandavate
B) Home Minister Mufti Mohammad Sayeed
C) External Affairs Minister I.K. Gujral
D) Deputy Prime Minister Devi Lal
questions.explanation: Prime Minister V.P. Singh announced the implementation of the Mandal report just days after sacking his powerful peasant deputy Devi Lal, outmaneuvering his rural factional challenger.

questions.question: The Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (PMGKAY), which provided 5 kg of free foodgrains per person per month to over 80 crore beneficiaries, was introduced in response to:
options: A) The COVID-19 pandemic and national lockdown in March 2020
B) The 2008 global financial crisis
C) The 2016 demonetization exercise
D) The 1999 Kargil conflict
questions.explanation: PMGKAY was announced on 26 March 2020 as part of the relief package during the COVID-19 national lockdown to ensure food security for poor households.

questions.topic: Cold War Era and Non-aligned Movement
questions.question: The Soviet Union was specifically impelled to establish the Warsaw Pact military alliance in May 1955 in direct response to:
options: A) The detonation of the first British hydrogen bomb in the Pacific
B) The admission and rearmament of the Federal Republic of Germany (West Germany) into NATO
C) The conclusion of the Korean War armistice at Panmunjom
D) The establishment of the United Nations Disarmament Commission
questions.explanation: When West Germany was officially admitted into NATO and allowed to rearm on 9 May 1955, the Soviet Union retaliated five days later by signing the Warsaw Pact on 14 May 1955.

questions.question: In December 1987, Mikhail Gorbachev and Ronald Reagan signed the Intermediate-Range Nuclear Forces (INF) Treaty, which was historic because it was the first treaty to:
options: A) Place a numerical cap on future production of intercontinental ballistic missiles
B) Ban underground nuclear testing across the polar ice caps
C) Completely eliminate an entire category of nuclear weapons (ground-launched missiles with ranges of 500 to 5,500 km)
D) Transfer all nuclear warheads to the United Nations Security Council
questions.explanation: Unlike previous treaties that capped or reduced arms, the 1987 INF Treaty banned and eliminated an entire class of nuclear weapons (intermediate- and shorter-range missiles), destroying over 2,600 missiles.

questions.question: The US-led coalition military assault Operation Desert Storm began with a massive air bombardment campaign on 16 January 1991, following the expiration of the deadline set by:
options: A) UN General Assembly Resolution 377A
B) UN Security Council Resolution 242
C) The NATO North Atlantic Council
D) UN Security Council Resolution 678
questions.explanation: UNSC Resolution 678 (passed in November 1990) gave Iraq until 15 January 1991 to withdraw from Kuwait or face 'all necessary means', authorizing the coalition assault that began hours later.

questions.question: Physical Euro currency banknotes and coins officially entered public circulation across participating European Union member states on:
options: A) 1 January 2002
B) 1 January 1999
C) 7 February 1992
D) 1 May 2004
questions.explanation: While adopted for electronic accountancy in 1999, the Euro became everyday physical cash on 1 January 2002, replacing national currencies like the Deutsche Mark and French Franc.

questions.question: Following the admission of Afghanistan at the 14th New Delhi Summit in 2007, the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) has how many member states?
options: A) Five member states
B) Eight member states
C) Ten member states
D) Twelve member states
questions.explanation: SAARC expanded from its original seven members (Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan, Sri Lanka) to eight when Afghanistan joined in April 2007.

questions.question: In September-October 1947, prior to launching the tribal incursion into Jammu & Kashmir, how did the Government of Pakistan violate the Standstill Agreement signed with Maharaja Hari Singh?
options: A) It formally requested the United Nations Trusteeship Council to annex the Kashmir valley.
B) It signed a joint naval military pact with the British Royal Navy to blockade Bombay.
C) It imposed an economic blockade, cutting off essential supplies of petrol, salt, wheat, and kerosene, and suspended postal and rail services to coerce accession.
D) It granted immediate citizenship to all state subjects residing in Jammu.
questions.explanation: Pakistan violated the Standstill Agreement by cutting off rail and road links from Rawalpindi and Sialkot, halting supplies of essential commodities to pressure the Maharaja into acceding.

questions.question: The Linguistic Provinces Commission (Dhar Commission) cautioned against reorganizing states primarily on linguistic lines in 1948 by warning that:
options: A) India would run out of steel to manufacture ballot boxes for provincial elections.
B) Linguistic states were explicitly prohibited by the Government of India Act, 1935.
C) The British Crown would automatically reclaim sovereignty over non-Hindi areas.
D) Linguistic provinces would foster regional chauvinism and create 'sub-nations', impeding the growth of a singular overarching Indian national identity.
questions.explanation: The Dhar Commission warned: 'Indian nationalism is yet in its infancy... linguistic provinces will have a sub-national bias and will militate against the development of an Indian nationality'.

questions.question: The historic 1957 Communist ministry in Kerala introduced the controversial Kerala Education Bill drafted by Education Minister Joseph Mundassery, which triggered the 'Vimochana Samaram' because:
options: A) It sought to regulate service conditions and salaries of teachers in private aided schools and audit school management funds, uniting the Catholic Church and Nair Service Society in protest.
B) It mandated the total abolition of all primary schools and forced children into collective farms.
C) It ordered all school textbooks to be printed in Russian instead of Malayalam.
D) It banned all Hindu temple festivals across the Malabar district.
questions.explanation: The bill aimed to protect teachers from exploitation by private school managements, but religious and community organizations viewed state oversight as an attack on minority rights, mobilizing the mass agitation that ousted the ministry.

questions.question: In the first general elections of 1952, the Bharatiya Jana Sangh secured only 3 seats in the Lok Sabha. In which states were these three seats won, reflecting its initial regional support base?
options: A) All three seats in Uttar Pradesh exclusively
B) Two seats in West Bengal (including Dr. Shyama Prasad Mukherjee) and one seat in Rajasthan
C) Two seats in Punjab and one seat in Gujarat
D) One seat in Bihar, one in Madhya Pradesh, and one in Maharashtra
questions.explanation: Dr. Shyama Prasad Mukherjee and Durga Charan Banerjee won from Calcutta South-East and Midnapore in West Bengal, while Barrister Umashankar Trivedi won from Chittor in Rajasthan, giving the BJS its 3 seats.

questions.question: Professor P.C. Mahalanobis developed which innovative mathematical and statistical methodology in the late 1950s to analyze disparities in household consumption and inequality across population deciles using NSS data?
options: A) Gini Coefficient Optimization
B) Input-Output Linear Matrix
C) Fractile Graphical Analysis
D) Stochastic Frontier Estimation
questions.explanation: Mahalanobis invented Fractile Graphical Analysis (FGA) in 1958, an ingenious non-parametric statistical technique to compare economic inequality and consumption patterns across regions and time.

questions.question: The Industrial Licensing Policy Inquiry Committee (Dutt Committee) submitted its report in 1969, revealing a major failure of early planning by demonstrating that:
options: A) All private corporate enterprises in India had gone bankrupt due to excessive labor strikes.
B) Public sector industries had completely eliminated the need for private consumer manufacturing.
C) Small cottage industries had expanded so rapidly that heavy steel plants were running at zero capacity.
D) The industrial licensing system had disproportionately favored large monopoly business houses (such as the Birlas and Tatas), who cornered licenses and blocked competitors.
questions.explanation: Subimal Dutt's committee showed that big business houses manipulated the licensing machinery to preempt industrial capacity and create monopolies, leading to the Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices (MRTP) Act of 1969.

questions.question: In late 1961, the Indian Government adopted the 'Forward Policy' along the disputed northern borders. What did this strategic directive entail?
options: A) Indian military posts were instructed to push forward into inter-post gaps and territory claimed by India in Ladakh and NEFA to interdict Chinese patrols, without adequate logistic support or defensive backup.
B) The Indian Navy was dispatched to capture Chinese merchant ships in the South China Sea.
C) India signed a mutual defense military pact with the United States to deploy tactical nuclear weapons.
D) All diplomatic embassies in Beijing and New Delhi were closed permanently.
questions.explanation: The Forward Policy established isolated, poorly supplied Indian outposts behind Chinese lines in Ladakh and along the McMahon Line on the assumption that China would not attack, creating vulnerable targets when war began.

questions.question: Under the Tashkent Declaration of 10 January 1966, India and Pakistan agreed to which crucial military withdrawal provision?
options: A) Pakistan surrendered all territorial claims over Azad Kashmir unconditionally.
B) Both sides agreed to withdraw all armed personnel by 25 February 1966 to the positions they held prior to 5 August 1965.
C) India agreed to evacuate all civil administration from the state of Punjab.
D) Both countries agreed to merge their air force commands under Soviet supervision.
questions.explanation: Article II of the Tashkent Declaration stipulated that both armed forces would withdraw to their pre-5 August 1965 positions, meaning India had to surrender strategic posts captured in Kashmir (like Haji Pir Pass).

questions.topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: In the dramatic 1969 presidential election, why was the counting of second-preference votes required to declare V.V. Giri elected?
options: A) Official candidate Sanjiva Reddy had passed away during the counting process.
B) The Supreme Court ordered an automatic recount due to a mechanical ballot box failure.

C) V.V. Giri secured 48% of the first-preference vote value, falling just short of the 50% quota; the elimination of third-candidate C.D. Deshmukh and transfer of his second preferences pushed Giri past the victory threshold.
D) Both candidates tied with exactly 300,000 value votes in the first round.
questions.explanation: Neither candidate secured an absolute majority of first-preference value votes (Giri: 401,515; Reddy: 313,948; Deshmukh: 112,764). When Deshmukh was eliminated, his second preferences favored Giri, giving him 420,077 and victory.

questions.topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: Enacted in November 1971 by Indira Gandhi's government following her landslide electoral victory, the 24th Constitutional Amendment Act aimed to:
options: A) Abolish the office of the President of India and create a permanent parliamentary directorate.
B) Privatize all state-owned commercial banks and restore royal privy purses.
C) Extend the tenure of the Lok Sabha from five years to ten years permanently.
D) Overturn the Supreme Court's 1967 Golaknath ruling by affirming Parliament's power to amend any part of the Constitution, including Fundamental Rights, under Article 368.
questions.explanation: The 24th Amendment amended Articles 13 and 368 to make clear that Parliament has the sovereign constituent power to amend any provision of the Constitution, including Fundamental Rights.

questions.question: In Minerva Mills v. Union of India (1980), the Supreme Court struck down Section 55 of the 42nd Amendment (which inserted Article 368(4) and (5) barring judicial review of amendments) because:
options: A) A limited amending power is itself a basic feature of the Constitution, and Parliament cannot convert a limited power into an unlimited power to destroy the Constitution.
B) The 42nd Amendment had not been signed by the President of India.
C) All constitutional amendments passed during an Emergency are automatically void ab initio.
D) The Supreme Court has no jurisdiction to interpret any article relating to fundamental duties.
questions.explanation: Chief Justice Y.V. Chandrachud famously ruled that Parliament cannot exercise its amending power to damage the Basic Structure: 'The donee of a limited power cannot by the exercise of that power convert the limited power into an unlimited one'.

questions.question: During the Emergency in January 1976, the Union Government dismantled independent news dissemination by forcibly amalgamating the four existing wire news agencies (PTI, UNI, Samachar Bharati, and Hindustan Samachar) into:
options: A) The Press Council of India
B) A single state-controlled monopoly news agency named 'Samachar'
C) The All India Radio News Directorate
D) The Central Board of Film Certification
questions.explanation: The four independent news agencies were coerced by the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting into merging into a single subsidized agency, 'Samachar', through which all government-vetted news was filtered.

questions.sub_topic: Rehabilitation of Army Deserters in Punjab Accord
questions.question: Which sensitive clause of the 1985 Rajiv-Longowal Accord addressed the grievances of Sikh soldiers who mutinied or deserted their units following Operation Blue Star?
options: A) Clause 4, granting immediate court-martial pardons and promoting all deserters to general ranks
B) Clause 4, transferring all mutinous soldiers to the direct command of the United Nations Peacekeeping Force
C) Clause 4, providing that those discharged from the Army will be rehabilitated and provided gainful civilian employment opportunities
D) Clause 4, revoking all military pension schemes across northern India
questions.explanation: Clause 4 provided that army personnel who had reacted emotionally to Operation Blue Star and were discharged would be rehabilitated and provided with civilian jobs.

questions.question: Clause 10 of the Assam Accord (1985) addressed the deep-seated grievances of indigenous tribal communities in Assam by stipulating that:
options: A) All tribal autonomous councils would be immediately dissolved and merged into the state cabinet.
B) Non-tribal settlers would be granted title deeds to all communal forest grazing lands.
C) Tribal languages would be completely replaced by Assamese in primary schools.
D) Existing laws for the protection of tribal belts and blocks will be strictly enforced, and unauthorized occupants will be evicted.
questions.explanation: Clause 10 committed the government to strictly protecting tribal lands in designated belts and blocks from encroachment by illegal immigrants or non-tribal settlers.

questions.question: The Chipko movement encompassed two divergent ideological strands regarding forest conservation. How did Sunderlal Bahuguna's perspective differ from Chandi Prasad Bhatt's perspective?
options: A) Bahuguna advocated a preservationist ecological approach seeking a total ban on tree felling, while Bhatt championed a community-development approach advocating sustainable local use of forest resources by village cooperatives.
B) Bahuguna favored commercial clear-felling by multinational companies, while Bhatt opposed all human presence in forests.
C) Bahuguna campaigned for converting all forests into urban shopping complexes, while Bhatt advocated planting commercial eucalyptus.
D) Both leaders completely rejected non-violence and called for an armed insurgency against forest guards.
questions.explanation: Bhatt's approach was utilitarian and livelihood-oriented (forests managed by local cooperatives for village industry), whereas Bahuguna's approach was preservationist and ecological (forests as soil/water conservers, demanding a complete logging ban).

questions.question: The sustained grassroots campaign of the Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan (MKSS) culminated in the passage of the Rajasthan Right to Information Act in May 2000, which served as a crucial catalyst because:
options: A) It repealed all provisions of the Indian Penal Code within the state of Rajasthan.
B) It demonstrated the administrative viability of statutory transparency, providing the empirical and legislative template for the national Right to Information Act, 2005.
C) It prohibited all government departments from maintaining written administrative files.
D) It was immediately struck down by the Supreme Court of India as a violation of official secrecy.
questions.explanation: The Rajasthan RTI Act 2000 proved that ordinary citizens could successfully audit state records, creating irresistible national momentum that led Parliament to enact the comprehensive central RTI Act in 2005.

questions.question: Which of the following was NOT among the three specific 'Social Indicators' (carrying the highest weight of 3 points each) formulated by the Mandal Commission?
options: A) Castes or classes considered as socially backward by others
B) Castes or classes which mainly depend on manual labor for their livelihood
C) Caste groups where the proportion of literate females is at least 25% below the state average
D) Castes or classes where at least 25% females and 10% males above the state average marry below the age of 17 in rural areas
questions.explanation: Female literacy below the state average was an Educational indicator (carrying 2 points), not a Social indicator. The three social indicators were: social perception by others, manual labor dependency, and early marriage rates.

questions.question: In his seminal study 'India's Silent Revolution', political scientist Christophe Jaffrelot argues that the post-Mandal era witnessed a fundamental democratic shift characterized by:
options: A) The complete replacement of civilian parliamentary democracy with military praetorian rule.
B) The total disappearance of caste identity from voting behavior and party competition.
C) A violent proletarian revolution that eliminated all private property ownership.
D) The transfer of political power from traditional upper-caste elites to lower castes (OBCs and Dalits) through democratic electoral representation in north India.
questions.explanation: Jaffrelot demonstrated that the implementation of the Mandal report catalyzed the rise of intermediate and lower castes to legislative power in the Hindi heartland, altering the sociological profile of Indian democracy.

questions.question: Empirical studies of voting behavior in the 2014 and 2019 Lok Sabha elections demonstrate that the BJP's electoral ascendancy was achieved by transforming its social base through:
options: A) Expanding beyond its historic urban upper-caste core to construct a broad cross-caste coalition incorporating lower/non-dominant OBCs and non-Jatav Dalits via welfare schemes and cultural nationalism.
B) Relying exclusively on the electoral support of industrial trade union workers in metropolitan cities.
C) Securing 100% of the vote share among religious minorities across southern states.
D) Boycotting rural agrarian constituencies to concentrate purely on university students.
questions.explanation: Lokniti-CSDS survey data show that the BJP under Narendra Modi broadened its footprint into a subaltern coalition, gaining substantial support from non-dominant backward castes and disadvantaged groups alongside upper castes.

questions.topic: Cold War Era and Non-aligned Movement
questions.question: Non-aligned and developing nations, including India, criticized the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT) as structurally hypocritical because while it strictly prohibited non-nuclear states from acquiring weapons, nuclear powers neglected Article VI, which mandated:
options: A) The mandatory sharing of all nuclear warhead blueprints with the United Nations General Assembly.
B) Pursuing negotiations in good faith on effective measures relating to cessation of the nuclear arms race at an early date and to nuclear disarmament.
C) The immediate transfer of nuclear submarines to coastal developing nations.
D) The compulsory shutdown of all commercial nuclear power reactors worldwide.
questions.explanation: Article VI of the NPT requires the P5 nuclear-weapon states to pursue complete nuclear disarmament, an obligation they largely ignored while enforcing non-proliferation on the rest of the world.

questions.question: When the leaders of Russia, Ukraine, and Belarus signed the Belavezha Accords on 8 December 1991 dissolving the USSR, what was their specific constitutional-legal justification?
options: A) They cited an executive order signed by United States President George H.W. Bush.
B) They invoked a binding directive issued by the Warsaw Pact Military Staff.
C) As the original surviving signatory states of the 1922 Treaty on the Creation of the USSR, they claimed the sovereign legal right to terminate the 1922 Treaty and dissolve the Union.
D) They enforced a unanimous resolution adopted by the Supreme Soviet of the USSR.
questions.explanation: Yeltsin, Kravchuk, and Shushkevich based their action on the fact that Russia, Ukraine, and Belarus were the original constituent co-founders of the Soviet Union in 1922, giving them the legal authority to dissolve it.

questions.question: In December 1994, Ukraine signed the historic Budapest Memorandum on Security Assurances, agreeing to relinquish the world's third-largest nuclear arsenal inherited from the USSR in return for:
options: A) Immediate full membership in the North Atlantic Treaty Organization with a permanent US military garrison.
B) The transfer of all Russian Black Sea naval fleet warships unconditionally to the Ukrainian Navy.
C) A permanent annual financial grant of $100 billion from the European Central Bank.
D) Commitments from Russia, the United States, and the United Kingdom to respect its independence, sovereignty, and existing borders, and to refrain from the threat or use of force.
questions.explanation: In the 1994 Budapest Memorandum, Ukraine surrendered over 1,900 strategic nuclear warheads, while Russia, the US, and the UK gave security assurances to respect Ukraine's independence and territorial sovereignty.

questions.question: In their influential structural analysis 'World Out of Balance' (2008), international relations scholars Stephen Brooks and William Wohlforth argue that US hegemony differs from all past historical empires because:
options: A) The gap between the United States and the second-ranking power across all four dimensions of power (military, economic, technological, and geographic) is so vast that traditional balancing by rivals is structurally unfeasible.
B) The United States has physically conquered and occupied every sovereign nation on Earth.
C) The United States possesses 100% of the world's total land area and natural resources.
D) All other sovereign nations have voluntarily dissolved their armed forces.
questions.explanation: Brooks and Wohlforth demonstrated that US unipolarity is multidimensional and unprecedented: the US leads simultaneously in military spending, naval dominance, technological innovation, and economic scale, rendering conventional balancing futile.

questions.question: On 1 May 2004, the European Union executed its historic 'Big Bang' enlargement by admitting ten new member countries simultaneously. Eight of these ten nations were former communist states of Eastern Europe; which were the other two?
options: A) Iceland and Norway
B) Cyprus and Malta
C) Switzerland and Liechtenstein
D) Turkey and Israel
questions.explanation: The 2004 enlargement admitted Poland, Czech Republic, Slovakia, Hungary, Slovenia, Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania, alongside the two Mediterranean island states of Cyprus and Malta.

questions.question: In 1999, the Chinese government launched the 'Going Out' policy (Zouchuqu), which marked a major strategic inflection point in China's external economic strategy by:
options: A) Ordering all Chinese citizens residing abroad to return immediately to the mainland.
B) Banning all foreign export trade and closing coastal ports to international container shipping.
C) Encouraging Chinese state-owned enterprises and private corporations to invest overseas, acquire global natural resources, and build international supply chains.
D) Surrendering management of Chinese state industries to the International Monetary Fund.
questions.explanation: The 'Going Out' strategy shifted China from being merely an importer of foreign direct investment to a massive global outbound investor, paving the way for Chinese multinational corporations and the Belt and Road Initiative.

questions.question: The decade-long civil war in Nepal that claimed over 17,000 lives was officially brought to an end in November 2006 through the signing of the Comprehensive Peace Accord (CPA) between:
options: A) King Gyanendra and the Secretary-General of the United Nations
B) The Chief of Army Staff and the President of the Supreme Court of Nepal
C) The Prime Minister of India and the Foreign Minister of China
D) Prime Minister Girija Prasad Koirala (representing the Government) and Chairman Prachanda (representing the CPN-Maoist)
questions.explanation: Signed on 21 November 2006, the CPA brought the Maoist rebels into the political mainstream, placed weapons under UN supervision, and led to the election of a Constituent Assembly that abolished the monarchy.

questions.question: Critics argue that regional integration under SAARC has been structurally crippled in comparison to ASEAN or the EU because Article X(1) of the SAARC Charter mandates that:
options: A) Decisions at all levels must be taken on the basis of unanimity, granting every single member state an absolute veto over any regional initiative.
B) Decisions are made by a simple majority vote weighted by national defense budgets.
C) The Republic of India holds a permanent executive veto over all trade resolutions.
D) All economic treaties must be approved by the United Nations Economic and Social Council.
questions.explanation: The requirement for complete unanimity means that any single member (such as Pakistan or India) can veto initiatives, stalling regional connectivity, trade pacts, and summit meetings.

questions.question: In the United Nations Security Council reform debates, which international coalition of countries (the 'Coffee Club') opposes the addition of new permanent members with veto power, advocating instead for the expansion of non-permanent elected seats?
options: A) The Group of Four (G4)
B) Uniting for Consensus (UFC), led by Italy, Pakistan, Mexico, Argentina, and South Korea
C) The African Union Peace and Security Council
D) The Non-Aligned Movement Coordinating Bureau
questions.explanation: The Uniting for Consensus group (comprising regional rivals of the G4, such as Pakistan against India, Italy against Germany, Mexico/Argentina against Brazil) opposes new permanent seats, arguing they make the Council less democratic.

questions.question: In contemporary security studies, the 'Securitization Theory' formulated by Barry Buzan and Ole Wæver of the Copenhagen School posits that an issue becomes a 'security threat' when:
options: A) A foreign sovereign state launches a confirmed nuclear missile attack against a naval vessel.
B) The International Criminal Court issues a formal indictment against an elected head of state.
C) A political actor presents an issue as an existential threat through a 'speech act', justifying the adoption of extraordinary emergency measures that bypass normal democratic debate.
D) An issue is declared a non-issue by unanimous agreement in the UN General Assembly.
questions.explanation: Securitization is an intersubjective process: threats are not just objective military realities, but are politically constructed when an actor successfully claims an existential threat to justify extraordinary powers.

questions.question: Article 1 of the 1992 Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) sets forth three comprehensive objectives. Which of the following accurately identifies these three objectives?
options: A) The eradication of all wild predator species, the expansion of chemical pesticides, and the privatization of genetic patents.
B) The creation of international marine commercial fisheries, deep-sea mining exploration, and space agriculture.
C) The compulsory relocation of all indigenous tribes into urban centers to protect wildlife.
D) The conservation of biological diversity, the sustainable use of its components, and the fair and equitable sharing of the benefits arising out of the utilization of genetic resources.
questions.explanation: The CBD's three interlocking goals are conservation, sustainable use, and access and benefit-sharing (ABS), which later led to the 2010 Nagoya Protocol on Genetic Resources.

questions.question: In his seminal 1995 book 'Jihad vs. McWorld', political theorist Benjamin Barber argued that contemporary globalization is defined by the dialectical collision between which two anti-democratic forces?
options: A) 'McWorld' (homogenizing global consumer capitalism and corporate commercialism) and 'Jihad' (parochial, fragmented, and retribalized religious and ethnic fundamentalism)
B) Socialist central state planning and Western Christian theological orthodoxy
C) International maritime law and space satellite commercial communication networks
D) National constitutional judiciaries and municipal civil service secretariats
questions.explanation: Barber argued that global corporate consumerism ('McWorld') and reactive ethnic/religious fundamentalism ('Jihad') reinforce each other while both undermining the civic foundations of participatory democracy.

questions.question: The linguistic reorganization of Punjab in 1966 that created the separate states of Punjab and Haryana was based on the recommendations of the Punjab Boundary Commission headed by:
options: A) Justice Fazal Ali
B) Justice S.K. Dhar
C) Justice K.K. Mathew
D) Justice J.C. Shah
questions.explanation: In April 1966, the Union Government appointed the Punjab Boundary Commission under Justice J.C. Shah (along with S. Dutt and M.M. Philip), which recommended creating Punjabi-speaking Punjab, Hindi-speaking Haryana, and making Chandigarh a Union Territory.
